items.definition:
a substance used to fill a space or cavity
The dentist put a new filling in my tooth.

a thin, transparent fabric used for dressings
The nurse wrapped the wound with sterile gauze.

an electrical device allowing two-way communication
Please use the intercom to speak to the receptionist.

A former monetary unit of Italy and other countries.
Before the euro, Italy's currency was the lira, plural lire.

A blend of spices used in Indian cooking.
Chicken tikka masala is a popular dish.

Lack of sensation in a part of the body.
He experienced numbness in his fingers after the cold exposure.

A factory where logs are sawn into timber.
The old sawmill stood by the river, silent and abandoned.

A display, exhibition, or performance.
The art gallery is having a showing of new local artists.

a severe snowstorm
The snowstorm caused widespread power outages.

a person or device that sweeps
The street sweeper cleans the roads every morning.

meat from a deer
For dinner, they served roasted venison with berry sauce.

friend (Spanish loanword)
He greeted his friend with a warm 'Hola, amigo!'

a person whose job is to keep records of the financial affairs of a business
Our bookkeeper manages all the company's accounts.

a powerful tractor with a broad blade at the front for pushing earth and debris
A bulldozer was used to clear the construction site.

a variety of black grape used for making red wine, or the wine itself
We ordered a bottle of Cabernet Sauvignon with dinner.

a type of plain-woven cotton fabric, or a cat with a mottled coat of black, orange, and white
She sewed the quilt from calico fabric.

a projection on the sole of a shoe or boot to provide grip
The soccer player's cleats dug into the grass.

the quality of being cute
The puppy's cuteness was irresistible.

a term of endearment, darling
Come here, darlin', and tell me what's wrong.

a Greek dish of meat cooked on a vertical spit
I ordered a delicious lamb gyro for lunch.

kilt
Many Scottish men wear a kilt for special occasions.

locket (a small ornamental case worn around the neck, holding a picture or lock of hair)
She wore a silver locket with a picture of her grandmother inside.

A person who has recently married.
The newlyweds left for their honeymoon immediately after the reception.

A long, narrow way or passage, especially in a building.
We walked down the long passageway to reach the main hall.

A sauce of crushed basil leaves, pine nuts, garlic, Parmesan cheese, and olive oil.
I made pasta with homemade pesto for dinner.

A large rodent with a coat of stiff, sharp quills.
Be careful not to get too close to the porcupine; its quills are sharp.

the quality or state of being short
He complained of shortness of breath.

A person who pays for and receives regular meals and lodging at another's house or in a school.
The school has many international boarders.

A pair of small drums joined together, played with the hands.
He played the bongo drums with great rhythm.

a female cowboy
The little girl dressed up as a cowgirl for Halloween.

a thin pancake
We had sweet crepes with fruit and whipped cream for dessert.

an action or thing that continues or completes a previous one
We need to do a followup on that meeting.

a small vehicle with a forked platform at the front that can be raised and lowered for loading, unloading, and moving things
The worker used a forklift to move the heavy crates.

a small, swift antelope with large eyes
A gazelle can run very fast to escape predators.

a burrowing rodent native to North and Central America
A gopher dug a tunnel under our garden.

a private house offering accommodation to paying guests
We stayed in a charming guesthouse near the beach.

a machine or person that harvests crops
The combine harvester worked tirelessly in the fields.

a form of indigestion felt as a burning sensation in the chest
Eating spicy food often gives me heartburn.

a wild dog-like animal found in Africa and Asia
A jackal howled in the distance under the desert moon.

a control stick for a video game or aircraft
He used the joystick to control the airplane in the flight simulator.

a small, brightly colored bird with a long, sharp beak, typically found near water
We spotted a beautiful kingfisher diving for fish in the river.

a tropical fruit with sweet, orange flesh
She enjoyed a slice of fresh papaya for breakfast.

a smooth, creamy paste made from cooked food
She made a delicious apple puree for the baby.

a venomous American snake
We saw a rattlesnake coiled on the hiking trail.

an Italian dish of rice cooked in broth
For dinner, we had a creamy mushroom risotto.

a three-leaf clover, especially associated with Ireland
Many people wear a shamrock on St. Patrick's Day.

the front part of a store
The old storefront was renovated with new windows.

a yellow-brown gemstone
She wore a necklace with a beautiful blue topaz.

a yellow spice
Turmeric is often used in Indian cuisine.

a grip or hold (used in "get ahold of")
I need to get ahold of him urgently.

the pointed tip of an arrow
He found an ancient arrowhead near the river.

a stroke played with the back of the hand facing the direction of the stroke
Her tennis backhand is very powerful.

a game played on a table with balls and cues (often plural "billiards")
He enjoys playing billiards in his free time.

a short, intensive training course
She joined a coding boot camp to learn programming quickly.

a person who comes, especially a newcomer
The young comer quickly made a name for himself in the industry.

a chemical or natural substance added to soil to increase its fertility
Farmers use fertiliser to improve crop yields.

articles made of glass
Be careful when washing the delicate glassware.

High-Definition Television
We bought a new HDTV for the living room.

The little finger.
He held up his pinkie to make a pinkie promise.

A horse bred and trained for racing.
The racehorse galloped towards the finish line.

an inhabitant of a town
The townspeople gathered in the square for the festival.

a test of the ability of a person or thing
She went to the tryouts for the school play.

a cigarette
He lit a cig after dinner.

a freshwater crustacean resembling a small lobster
We caught some crayfish in the river.
